content.title: Jason Day's majors timeline: Breaking down golfer's last major win and more | Sporting News
content.text: For over a decade, Jason Day has been among the world's best golfers.The Australian ranked first in the world in 2015, building an up-and-coming career. However, Day had a winless drought for some time and has been unable to break through as one of golf's true premier names. In recent years, Day has gotten back on track, re-entering the world's top 20 golfers. And at the 2025 Masters, he was one of the top performers over the first two rounds and finished tied for eighth.📲 Follow The Sporting News on WhatsAppHere's what to know about Day's major victories.MORE: Tracking the 2025 Masters cut lineHow many majors has Jason Day won?Day has one major championship, the 2015 PGA Championship. He has had plenty of second-place finishes at other major tournaments, but hasn't been able to secure another win.SN's MASTERS HQ: Live Masters leaderboard | Masters TV coverage | Live streamingWhen was the last time Jason Day won a major?The last time Day won a major was his lone victory, the 2015 PGA Championship. In that competition, he shot rounds of 68, 67, 66 and 67 to beat out Jordan Speith by three strokes.With that win, Day also became the first golfer in history to finish 20 under par in a major.Has Jason Day won the Masters?Day has never won the Masters. The 2025 tournament is his 14th time competing in Augusta, but he has come close to earning a green jacket.In 2011, Day made his first Masters start and finished tied for second with a -12, setting a new tournament record for the lowest score by a first-time participant. In 2013, he was tied for the lead at various points of the Masters but finished in third place, two shots back of the winner, Adam Scott.Day hasn't finished in the top three of the Masters since then. In 2016, he finished tied for 10th and in 2019, he tied for fifth. Day has made the cut in 10 of his previous 13 Masters appearances.Here are Day's results at Augusta by year:Jason Day's Masters historyYearFinishTotal2011T22762012-76 (one round)201332812014T202902015T282872016T102892017T222902018T202862019T52772020-148 (two rounds)2021-153 (two rounds)2023T392932024T302932025T8283MORE: Why the Masters are always in AugustaJason Day majors timelineDay played in his first major at the 2010 Open Championship, making the cut and tying for 60th place. Later that year, he competed in his first PGA Championship, and he had a seven-under par for his first top-10 finish in a major.The 2011 Masters was Day's breakthrough, finishing second; it's his best finish in Augusta to date. Day's first U.S. Open appearance also came in 2011, finishing second behind Rory McIlroy. Although he had yet to win a major, the consistency earned Day a top-10 appearance in the World Golf Rating.For the second time, Day finished tied as the runner-up at the 2013 U.S. Open. He was two strokes behind the winner, Justin Rose.In the 2015 Open Championship, Day continued to find success while barely coming up short of a win. By tying for fourth, it was the sixth time he had finished in the top-5 of a major without winning. Fortunately, his first victory came later that season, winning the 2015 PGA Championship.In 2023, Day finished second at the Open Championship — meaning that at some point, he had finished second in all four majors, a "runner-up grand slam."Here's a look at Day's second-place finishes in majors:YearMajorFinishScore2011MastersT2-122011U.S. Open2-82016PGA Championship2-132023Open ChampionshipT2-7
